payload.rationale: The forecast depends heavily on the expected contribution of gasoline prices and the underlying core inflation rate. Early September EIA data shows a sharp increase in gasoline prices, which, combined with recent core inflation trends, strongly suggests a headline CPI print of 0.3% or higher.
limitations: Only early September gasoline data is available; late-month price drops could alter the energy contribution.
Core inflation components, such as shelter and used cars, can be volatile and unpredictable.
Seasonal adjustment factors can introduce unexpected revisions or adjustments to the unadjusted data.
payload.partition_justification: The scenarios are partitioned based on the behavior of core inflation and the trajectory of energy prices in the remainder of September. These two factors are the primary drivers of headline CPI variance in the short term.

scenarios.description: Core CPI remains steady at 0.3% or higher, and gasoline prices maintain their early September gains or rise further.
scenarios.rationale: With a core CPI of 0.3% and a positive energy contribution of ~0.15% to 0.20%, headline CPI would easily reach 0.4% or 0.5%, well above the 0.2% threshold.
unknowns: Exact core CPI print for September

scenarios.description: Core CPI cools to 0.1% or 0.2%, but the early September gasoline price spike sustains, adding a positive energy contribution.
scenarios.rationale: Even with a cooler core, the ~4-5% increase in gasoline prices (contributing ~0.15% to headline) would likely push the rounded headline CPI to 0.3%.

scenarios.description: Core CPI drops significantly (below 0.1%) or late September gasoline prices plummet, erasing the early month gains.
scenarios.rationale: If energy prices reverse sharply or core inflation unexpectedly stalls, headline CPI could print at 0.2% or lower. However, the strong early-month gasoline data makes this less likely.
